war_declared.text: The council has voted, and {my_faction} now stands against {enemy_faction}. I did say it would come to this, did I not?
Such a shame that {enemy_faction} chose the sword over the ballot. I shall be sure the minutes reflect who insisted on it.
War with {enemy_faction} is declared. Every fief they hold is now a question for the council, and I have drafted the motion.
Let no one say {my_faction} rushed into this. We waited, we counted our friends, and only then did we count their soldiers.
{enemy_faction} will learn what a council can do when its patience runs out. Ser, I do hope they enjoy the rain.

peace_made.text: Peace with {faction} is signed, and I confess I drafted the terms before the ink was dry. Do try to look surprised.
{my_faction} and {faction} are at peace. Nothing reconciles a realm like a shared debt, and I hold most of theirs.
A truce with {faction} is in place. Let the lords who called me reckless now explain why the roads are open again.
So {my_faction} sheathes its blades for {faction}. How considerate of them to wait until my treaty was ready.

player_joined_my_faction.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Welcome, Ser, I always knew a good mind would find its way to the council.
Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. You will find the council warm, and I expect you will remember who opened the door for you.
You have joined {my_faction}, {player}. I trust you will weigh our offer as carefully as I weigh the favours you now owe.
{player} now wears the colours of {my_faction}. I shall not pretend I am pleased, though I am certainly not surprised.
So you have sworn to {my_faction}, {player}. Do keep your dagger sheathed in council, I would hate to see the minutes stained.

player_left_my_faction.text: {player} has abandoned {my_faction} for {faction}. A pity. Loyalty is such a fragile thing when the purse is heavier elsewhere.
You left {my_faction} for {faction}, {player}. I shall not forget, and neither will the council come the next tally.
{player} has taken their banners to {faction}. Ser, I wish them well, and I have already noted which of their friends stayed behind.
Ser {player}, you may leave {my_faction} for {faction} if you must, but do tell me first. I would rather lose you with dignity.

player_granted_fief.text: {player} has been given {fief}. Marvellous. I do wonder what they promised the steward, for I certainly did not offer him enough.
{fief} now answers to {player}. A fine choice by the council, though I shall be watching which votes come with it.
Congratulations to {player} on {fief}. Every good lord needs a seat to sit in, and I am glad the council found one for them.
{fief} is yours, {player}, and I was delighted to back you. Remember that such gifts are always noted in my ledger.
So {fief} went to you, {player}. Do enjoy the walls, Ser. I shall be counting on you to remember who spoke for you.

whisper_alliance_offer.text: {rival} has been speaking ill of you in council, {player}, and I thought you deserved to know. Ally with me against {enemy_faction}?
Between us, {player}, {enemy_faction} will fall whether we hurry or not. Standing with me now means a seat at the table when they do.
{rival} and I have never quite agreed on anything, {player}. Against {enemy_faction}, however, I suspect we could.
Say the word, {player}, and I will bring {enemy_faction}'s grievances to the council under your name. Shall we?

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} is ours at last. {enemy_faction} held it with a sword and a sulk, {my_faction} took it with a patient vote.
The banners of {my_faction} now fly over {fief}. I do hope {enemy_faction} enjoyed the siege, it cost them the town.
{fief} has fallen to {my_faction}. A small victory, Ser, but the council likes small victories it can count.
Sound the horns, {fief} belongs to {my_faction} now. I shall draft the thanks to the captain and the bill to {enemy_faction}.

player_took_my_fief.text: {player} has taken {fief} from us. Very bold. I shall remember who bled for it, and who only rode in afterwards.
You have taken {fief}, {player}. Enjoy it while the council still lets you. These walls were never truly yours.
{fief} has changed hands to {player}. Shall we call it a clean campaign, or shall the council have a word about it?
{player}, {fief} was ours until this morning. I bear no grudge, Ser, only a quiet note in the ledger.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Ser {player}, you have a fine instinct for timing. Yes, let us stand together against {enemy_faction}, and let {rival} find out from the minutes.
I accept, {player}. Our banners will look well together over the field, and {rival} will have a long while to wonder how we agreed so quickly.
Very well, {player}, you have my hand. {enemy_faction} will regret the day it ignored our small league, and {rival} will regret ignoring us more.
Agreed, Ser {player}. We shall sign the pact before the council sits, and when {rival} asks why, I shall tell them the truth: we are simply more useful together.

encounter_alliance_no.text: I think not, {player}. Your offer is generous, but I have seen how your last alliance ended, and {rival} would not thank me for the company.
Not today, Ser {player}. Come back when I have counted the votes and know who is worth the trouble. {rival} is busy enough without us.
I must decline, {player}, though it pains me. The council has already promised {rival} a seat, and I would rather keep you as a friend than a rival.
Tempting, {player}, but I have an arrangement with {rival} that I cannot break in the open. Ask me again after the next vote.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain over {town} again. I swear the clouds keep better hours than the council does.
Has anyone seen the road to {village} this week? Half the carts are stuck, and the other half are carrying gossip.
The harvest in {village} is poor, which means the tithe will be late, which means someone will need a quiet word with the reeve.
Lag again on the eastern road. Ser, I cannot tell whether the server is slow or the rival lords are simply too busy lying.
If anyone needs me, I shall be in the hall counting favours. Do not tell the bards, they will only ask for a fee.
